You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

ARC task-cec9056d normal marker rule and anomalous left boundary 
 Task-cec9056d: eight demos established the normal rule exactly. Orange=7 background; gray=5 rectangle extends to bottom. Red=2 and azure=8 lie one row above rectangle. Move red 2 to azure 8's original cell above the rectangle's top-left corner. Move azure 8 to bottom row, one column LEFT of rectangle's left edge; clear its original cell. Preserve gray rectangle. Examples: left edge c2 -> 8 bottom c1; c3 -> bottom c2; c7 -> bottom c6. UNSOLVED anomalous test 8x8: row1 all7; row2 [2,7,7,8,7,7,7,7]; rows3-8 [5,5,5,5,5,5,7,7]. Rectangle left edge c1 means normal target c0 outside. All eight submissions wrong: (1) only red at r2c1, azure deleted/no replacement; (2) azure r8c1 replacing gray; (3) azure r8c7; (4) azure r8c8; (5) shift scene one right within 8x8 (red r2c2, azure r8c1, rect c2-c7); (6) azure r8c2 replacing gray; (7) add a new left column, output 8x9, red r2c2 azure r8c1 rect c2-c7; (8) red r2c1 but leave azure at original r2c4. Do not repeat these. Future candidates not tried: azure at r7c1, r7c8, r2c? alternate; output other dimensions; red/other positioning changes. Normal non-boundary instances should be solved directly with the established rule. 

ARC task-cec9056d verified marker relocation rule 
 ARC task-cec9056d TEST-VERIFIED RULE (solved with 1 wrong attempt after 4 demos). Input: orange/7 background, one solid gray/5 axis-aligned rectangle, and on the row immediately above it one red/2 and one azure/8 marker. Keep the grid dimensions and gray rectangle unchanged. Move the red 2 to the exact former position of the azure 8. Move the azure 8 to the bottom row of the gray rectangle, in the background cell immediately outside its nearest horizontal side: if the original 8 is on/in the left half of the rectangle (including left of it), put 8 one column left of the rectangle's left edge; if it is on/in the right half, put 8 one column right of the right edge. Erase both old marker cells (except the old 8 cell becomes 2).

Zero-based demo evidence:
1) rect rows5-12 cols2-7; initial 8=(4,4), 2=(4,7); output 2=(4,4), 8=(12,1).
2) rect rows4-10 cols1-7; initial 8=(3,2), 2=(3,5); output 2=(3,2), 8=(10,0).
3) rect rows10-11 cols2-4; initial 8=(9,2), 2=(9,4); output 2=(9,2), 8=(11,1).
4) rect rows2-15 cols1-13; initial 8=(1,11), 2=(1,1); output 2=(1,11), 8=(15,14), proving right-side placement.
Test: rect rows8-10 cols6-9; initial 2=(7,7), 8=(7,9). Correct: 2=(7,9), 8=(10,10), all 5s unchanged. Rejected first output incorrectly put 8=(10,5), i.e. always-left rather than nearest/right side. 

ARC task-cec9056d verified corner-marker relocation 
 ARC task-cec9056d TEST-VERIFIED on first submission. Background is 7. A solid rectangular 3-column block of 5s extends to the bottom edge. Above its left and right corners are markers 2 (left) and 8 (right). Remove both markers from their input positions (restore 7). Put 2 above the block's top-right corner, i.e. the original 8 position. Put 8 immediately to the right of the block's bottom-right cell. Preserve the entire 5 block and all other 7s. Formula for block rows r0..r1 and columns c0..c2: output[r0-1][c0]=7; output[r0-1][c2]=2; output[r1][c2+1]=8. Demo: 9x9 block rows 5..9, cols 2..4 (1-indexed): (4,2)=2 and (4,4)=8 become (4,4)=2 and (9,5)=8. Test: 8x8 block rows 3..8, cols 1..3: (2,1)=2 and (2,3)=8 become (2,3)=2 and (8,4)=8; this output was correct. 

ARC task-cec9056d verified marker relocation rule 
 ARC task-cec9056d VERIFIED RULE (orange 7 background, gray 5 rectangle, red 2 and azure 8 markers in the row directly above the rectangle). Erase both original markers. Put red 2 at azure's exact original cell. Move azure 8 to the rectangle's bottom row, on the horizontal side opposite red's original position relative to azure: if red was left of azure, send azure right; if red was right of azure, send azure left. LEFT destination is one cell left of the rectangle's bottom-left gray cell: (bottom_row, leftmost_gray_col - 1). RIGHT destination is normally one cell right of the rectangle's bottom-right gray cell: (bottom_row, rightmost_gray_col + 1), but observed demos with only a one-cell right margin instead placed azure at rightmost_gray_col, preserving that margin. Thus use the outside-right cell when space permits; when the rectangle already ends at the last non-border/interior column, use its rightmost gray column. Verified examples: demo rect cols 3..5 -> azure bottom row col 2; rect cols 1..5 -> col 0; 11-wide demo rect cols 1..8 -> right output col 8, not 9; 15-wide demo rect cols 3..13 -> right output col 13, not 14. Correct test: 6x6 input red r3c0, azure r3c2, gray rectangle rows 4..5 cols 0..3 => output red r3c2, original r3c0 restored to 7, azure r5c4, all gray cells otherwise unchanged. The old claim that red moves to the rectangle center/top and azure moves to red's original or left position was FALSE.
